info.title: NaviPet API
info.description: Backend API for NaviPet indoor campus navigation.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description:
Signs in an existing, confirmed account and returns a session.

Public — no bearer token is needed. The email is trimmed and lowercased before it is checked.

---

Send the returned `access_token` as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every protected route.

---

Keep `refresh_token` for `POST /auth/refresh` once the access token expires.

A newly registered account cannot sign in until its emailed code has been confirmed through `POST /auth/verify-otp`.

200.description: Tokens issued. Do not store the refresh token in browser localStorage.

schema.description: Tokens issued. Do not store the refresh token in browser localStorage.

401.description: Email or password is incorrect. Also returned for an unknown email, so the response cannot be used to discover which accounts exist.

schema.description: Email or password is incorrect. Also returned for an unknown email, so the response cannot be used to discover which accounts exist.

403.description: Credentials were valid, but the account is disabled.

schema.description: Credentials were valid, but the account is disabled.

post.summary: Register with first name, last name, email, and password
post.description:
Creates an unconfirmed account and emails it a 6-digit verification code.

Public — no bearer token is needed. This call never returns access or refresh tokens.

Names and email are trimmed, and the email is lowercased, before validation.

The password needs 8 to 128 characters with at least one digit and one special character.

---

Next step: submit the emailed code to `POST /auth/verify-otp` with `type: "register"`. That call confirms the account and signs it in.

200.description: Registration accepted. Supabase requires email confirmation, so no session or tokens are issued until the user submits the verification code emailed to them to POST /auth/verify-otp (type: 'register').

enum: Verification code sent. Check your inbox.

post.summary: Rotate a refresh token for a new access/refresh pair
post.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access/refresh pair.

Public — no bearer token is needed. Call it once the current access token expires.

The response replaces both tokens. The submitted `refreshToken` is consumed and cannot be used again.

Reusing an already-consumed refresh token returns 401 and revokes its entire token family, so always retry with the newest token.

A recovery session from `POST /auth/verify-otp` cannot be refreshed and also returns 401.

schema.description: The refresh token is missing, unknown, expired, or was already used. Reuse of a consumed token revokes its entire token family.

post.description:
Signs out the session that the bearer access token belongs to.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Takes no request body.

Only that session is revoked — the same user stays signed in on other devices. Use `POST /auth/logout-all` to end every session.

To test: sign in, paste `access_token` into the "Authorize" button in Swagger UI, then execute.

A repeat call for an already-revoked session still returns 204.

post.summary: Revoke every session for the authenticated user
post.description:
Signs the authenticated user out everywhere.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Takes no request body.

Unlike `POST /auth/logout`, this revokes every session the user has on every device.

Afterwards no previously issued token pair works; the user must sign in again with `POST /auth/login`.

get.description:
Returns the account that the bearer access token belongs to.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

Use it to check that a token still works and to read the account id, email, status, and creation time.

A bad or expired token returns 401. A valid token returns 403 when the account has been disabled and 404 when it has been deleted.

post.summary: Request a password reset verification code by email
post.description:
First step of password recovery: emails a 6-digit verification code to an existing account.

Public — no bearer token is needed. The email is trimmed and lowercased before the lookup.

An email with no account returns 404. This is a deliberate product choice; `POST /auth/login` hides whether an account exists.

---

Next step: submit the emailed code to `POST /auth/verify-otp` with `type: "recovery"`.

200.description: A matching account was found and a verification code was sent.

enum: Verification code sent. Check your inbox.

schema.description: A matching account was found and a verification code was sent.

schema.description: No account exists for this email.

schema.description: Please enter a valid email address.

schema.description: Password reset is unavailable (Supabase admin credentials not configured).

post.summary: Send a confirmation code to change the sign-in email
post.description:
Starts an email-address change for the authenticated user.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` from a session that signed in with a password in the last 10 minutes.

An older session gets a 401 with code `REAUTH_REQUIRED`. Call `POST /auth/login` again and retry with the new token.

---

The email is trimmed and lowercased. A 6-digit code is sent to the new address only.

The response is the same 202 whether or not the address already belongs to another account, so it cannot be used to look up accounts.

---

Next step: submit the code through `POST /auth/verify-otp` with the new address as `email` and `type: "email_change"`.

202.description: The request was accepted. If the address can be used, a 6-digit code is on its way to it.

schema.description: The request was accepted. If the address can be used, a 6-digit code is on its way to it.

401.description: Access token is missing, invalid, or expired (`INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN`), or the session has no recent password sign-in (`REAUTH_REQUIRED`).

schema.description: Access token is missing, invalid, or expired (`INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN`), or the session has no recent password sign-in (`REAUTH_REQUIRED`).

422.description: The new email is malformed or matches the current email.

schema.description: The new email is malformed or matches the current email.

post.summary: Verify a one-time code for password reset, signup, or email change
post.description:
Confirms an emailed 6-digit code and returns a session. One endpoint serves three flows, selected by `type`.

Public — no bearer token is needed. Use the "Examples" dropdown on the request body below to load a sample payload for any flow.

---

### Password reset — `type: "recovery"`

**Step 1.** `POST /auth/forgot-password` with `{ "email" }`.

**Step 2.** Read the 6-digit code from that inbox.

**Step 3.** `POST /auth/verify-otp` with `{ "email", "code", "type": "recovery" }`.

**Step 4.** Use the returned `access_token` as the Bearer credential on `POST /auth/reset-password`.

This is a recovery session: it works only for the password reset. Other protected routes reject it with 401, and it cannot be refreshed.

---

### Signup email confirmation — `type: "register"`

**Step 1.** `POST /auth/register` with the new account details.

**Step 2.** Read the 6-digit code from that inbox.

**Step 3.** `POST /auth/verify-otp` with `{ "email", "code", "type": "register" }`.

**Step 4.** The account is now confirmed and the returned tokens are a normal session. No separate `POST /auth/login` call is needed.

---

### Confirm an email change — `type: "email_change"`

**Step 1.** `POST /auth/change-email` with the new address and the current bearer token.

**Step 2.** Read the 6-digit code sent to the new address.

**Step 3.** Call this endpoint with the new address as `email`, the code, and `"type": "email_change"`.

**Step 4.** The sign-in email is now the new address. Replace the stored tokens with the returned session so the token carries the new email.

**Step 5.** Show the returned message to the user: the new address is the one to sign in with from now on.

---

A wrong code and an expired code return the same 401 in every flow, so the response never reveals whether a code was ever valid.

type.description: 'recovery' verifies a password reset code (from /auth/forgot-password); 'register' verifies an email confirmation code (from /auth/register); 'email_change' verifies the code sent to a new address (from /auth/change-email).

email_change.description: Code sent to the new address by POST /auth/change-email. `email` is the new address.

200.description: A session for the verified account. For type: recovery this is a short-lived recovery session — send the access_token as a bearer credential to POST /auth/reset-password to set a new password. For type: register this is a normal login session — the account is now confirmed and signed in. For type: email_change this is a normal login session whose email claim is the new address — replace the stored tokens with it.

message.description: Present only for type: email_change. Tells the user which email to use at the next sign-in.
message.example: Email updated. Use this email the next time you sign in.

schema.description: A session for the verified account. For type: recovery this is a short-lived recovery session — send the access_token as a bearer credential to POST /auth/reset-password to set a new password. For type: register this is a normal login session — the account is now confirmed and signed in. For type: email_change this is a normal login session whose email claim is the new address — replace the stored tokens with it.

post.summary: Set a new password using a verified recovery session
post.description:
Last step of password recovery: sets a new password.

Requires a recovery `access_token` as the Bearer credential. A normal login token is rejected with 401.

---

To test: call `POST /auth/forgot-password`, then `POST /auth/verify-otp` with `type: "recovery"`.

---

Paste the `access_token` from that response into the "Authorize" button, then send matching `newPassword` and `confirmPassword`.

---

The password needs 8 to 128 characters with at least one uppercase letter and one digit, and must differ from the previous one.

A successful reset signs the user out everywhere, including this recovery session. Sign in again with `POST /auth/login`.

204.description: Password changed. No response body. The recovery session used for this request and the user's other active sessions are revoked.

schema.description: Password changed. No response body. The recovery session used for this request and the user's other active sessions are revoked.

401.description: The recovery access token is missing, invalid, or expired.

schema.description: The recovery access token is missing, invalid, or expired.

422.description: newPassword/confirmPassword failed validation, either schema validation (too short, missing an uppercase letter or a digit), a mismatch between the two fields, or a Supabase-side check (e.g. the new password matches the previous one).

schema.description: newPassword/confirmPassword failed validation, either schema validation (too short, missing an uppercase letter or a digit), a mismatch between the two fields, or a Supabase-side check (e.g. the new password matches the previous one).

get.description:
Searches active, searchable CSULB campus destinations that match `q`.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

`q` must contain at least two meaningful characters, otherwise the request returns 422.

`limit` defaults to 10 and is capped at 20.

`latitude` and `longitude` are optional but must be sent together.

---

### Proximity search

These phrases search for the nearest matching places instead of matching by name: "nearest restroom", "food near me", "nearest parking", "closest bus stop", "coffee near me".

They require `latitude` and `longitude`; without them the request returns 422.

---

Only places within 2000 meters are returned, each with `distanceMeters`, and the response gains a `proximity` object.

---

### Mapbox fallback

When an ordinary search finds no campus destination with outdoor coordinates, a temporary Mapbox result may be returned instead. Proximity searches never do this.

A Mapbox result has `external: true` and an `id` starting with `mapbox:`.

---

It is not stored, so that `id` cannot be used with `GET /places/{placeId}` or `POST /recent-searches`.

get.description:
Returns one active, searchable campus destination by its UUID.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

`placeId` is the `id` of a campus result from `GET /autocomplete`.

---

A well-formed UUID with no matching active, searchable destination returns 404.

A temporary Mapbox result has a `mapbox:` prefixed `id`, which is not a UUID and returns 422.

---

For those, use the coordinates already present on the autocomplete result.

get.summary: Search verified rooms in a building
get.description:
Searches the rooms inside one building, best match for `q` first.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

`buildingCode` is the campus building code, for example "ECS". It is matched case-insensitively.

---

`q` must contain at least two meaningful characters. Whitespace inside it is ignored, so "101" and "1 01" match the same rooms.

`limit` defaults to 10 and is capped at 20.

Only active, searchable rooms are returned — never buildings, entrances, or other destination types.

A building code that does not resolve to an active, searchable building returns 404.

`latitude` and `longitude` are accepted but ignored here.

post.description:
Records that the authenticated user picked a campus place, so it appears in `GET /recent-searches`.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Each user can read and write only their own list.

---

Send the `id` of a campus result from `GET /autocomplete` as `placeId`.

The place is looked up again on the server; the stored copy comes from the database, not from the request.

Saving a place that is already in the list refreshes its timestamp instead of adding a duplicate, so the call is safe to repeat.

A well-formed UUID with no matching place returns 404.

A temporary Mapbox result (`mapbox:` prefixed `id`) cannot be saved and returns 422.

401.description: Authentication is required.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's saved places, most recently searched first.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Each user sees only their own list.

Each entry carries the place fields plus a `searchedAt` timestamp.

`limit` defaults to 10 and is capped at 20.

A user with no history gets an empty array, not a 404.

delete.summary: Clear all recent selected campus places
delete.description:
Deletes every recent search that belongs to the authenticated user.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Takes no request body, and never touches another user's history.

There is no per-entry delete.

Clearing an already-empty history also returns 204.

`DELETE /recent-searches` and `DELETE /all-recent-searches` behave identically.

get.description:
Returns every class on the authenticated user's schedule, oldest first.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, using the `access_token` from `POST /auth/login`.

In Swagger UI, paste the token into the "Authorize" button; it is then sent with every request on this page.

A user with no classes gets an empty array.

building.description: A CSULB building name or code (e.g. "VEC" or "Vivian Engineering Center") is resolved against the campus dataset. Anything else (a street address, another campus, an off-campus site) is forward-geocoded with Mapbox instead. Either way the stored class gets a resolved display name plus latitude/longitude. Required for in-person classes. Optional for online classes, where it is stored as sent (possibly empty) and never resolved.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays the class meets: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.

isOnline.description: An online class has no physical location: no building is required and no coordinates are stored. A synchronous online class still occupies its time slot for conflict checks.

post.summary: Add a class to the authenticated user schedule
post.description:
Adds one class to the authenticated user's schedule.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. The example request body below works as sent.

### Location

`building` accepts a CSULB building name or code, or a plain street address.

Either way the saved class gets a resolved display name and coordinates, used later for class-aware navigation. A building or address that cannot be found returns 404.

Set `isOnline: true` for an online class; `building` may then be omitted or empty.

An in-person class with no `building` returns 422.

### Time

Send the time one of two ways: `time` as a CSULB range such as "4-6:45PM", or `startTime` with `endTime`.

---

Sending both forms, neither form, or a time that cannot be read returns 422.

An end time that is not later than the start time returns 422.

### Schedule conflicts

Two classes conflict when they share a weekday and their times overlap.

Back-to-back classes are allowed: one ending at 10:00 and one starting at 10:00 do not conflict.

A class with an empty `weekdays` list is asynchronous and never conflicts.

A conflicting or duplicate class is rejected with 409 and nothing is saved.

building.description: A CSULB building name or code (e.g. "VEC" or "Vivian Engineering Center") is resolved against the campus dataset. Anything else (a street address, another campus, an off-campus site) is forward-geocoded with Mapbox instead. Either way the stored class gets a resolved display name plus latitude/longitude. Required for in-person classes. Optional for online classes, where it is stored as sent (possibly empty) and never resolved.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays the class meets: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.

isOnline.description: An online class has no physical location: no building is required and no coordinates are stored. A synchronous online class still occupies its time slot for conflict checks.

startTime.description: Local start time: 24-hour "HH:MM" / "HH:MM:SS", or 12-hour "4:00 PM" / "4PM". Omit when sending `time`.

endTime.description: Local end time, same formats as `startTime`. Must be later than `startTime`. Omit when sending `time`.

time.description: A CSULB schedule time range such as "8-8:50AM", "12:30-3:15PM", "4-6:45PM", or "10:30AM-1:15PM". AM/PM written once applies to both ends unless the range crosses noon ("11-12:15PM" is 11:00 AM-12:15 PM). Replaces `startTime` + `endTime`. "NA/NA" (no scheduled time) is rejected with 422.

Anything else (a street address, another campus, an off-campus site) is forward-geocoded with Mapbox instead. Either way the stored class gets a resolved display name plus latitude/longitude. Required for in-person classes. Optional for online classes, where it is stored as sent (possibly empty) and never resolved.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays the class meets: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.

isOnline.description: An online class has no physical location: no building is required and no coordinates are stored. A synchronous online class still occupies its time slot for conflict checks.

patch.description:
Changes one class on the authenticated user's schedule.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

Send only the fields being changed. An empty body returns 422.

### Location

Omitting `building` leaves the stored location untouched.

Sending `building` resolves it again, the same way `POST /classes` does.

---

Setting `isOnline: true` clears the stored coordinates.

Setting `isOnline: false` resolves `building` — the one sent, else the stored one. An empty building returns 422.

### Time

`time` replaces both `startTime` and `endTime` and cannot be combined with either.

---

Changing `weekdays`, `time`, `startTime`, `endTime`, or `courseCode` re-checks the whole class.

---

The end time must stay later than the start time (422), and the class must not conflict with another class on the schedule (409).

### Schedule conflicts

Two classes conflict when they share a weekday and their times overlap.

Back-to-back classes are allowed: one ending at 10:00 and one starting at 10:00 do not conflict.

A class with an empty `weekdays` list is asynchronous and never conflicts.

A conflicting or duplicate class is rejected with 409 and nothing is saved.

Discards a temporary avatar upload, for when the user cancels their profile changes.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

`uploadId` is the value returned by `POST /profiles/me/avatar`.

Do not call this after that `uploadId` has been committed through `PATCH /profiles/me`.

get.description:
Returns the display name, email, role, and avatar of the authenticated user, as shown on the profile screen.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

`avatarUrl` is a temporary signed URL that expires after about one hour, so fetch the profile again rather than caching the URL.

`avatarUrl` is `null` when no avatar can be served; show a local placeholder instead.

patch.description:
Updates the profile of the authenticated user and returns the saved profile.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

Send at least one field. Omitted fields keep their current values.

`displayName` is trimmed and cannot be blank. To change the email, use `POST /auth/change-email`; email is deliberately not editable through this endpoint.

---

To save a new avatar, first call `POST /profiles/me/avatar`, then send its `uploadId` here as `avatarUploadId`.

---

The returned `avatarUrl` is a temporary signed URL that expires after about one hour.

In Swagger UI, delete the fields you do not want to change from the example body before executing.

post.description:
Uploads one image as a temporary avatar. It is not the saved profile avatar until it is committed.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

Send `multipart/form-data` with the file in a field named `avatar`.

Accepted formats are JPEG, PNG, and WebP, up to 5 MB.

---

**To keep it:** send the returned `uploadId` as `avatarUploadId` in `PATCH /profiles/me`.

---

**To discard it:** call `DELETE /profiles/me/avatar/{uploadId}`.

---

The returned `avatarUrl` is a preview link that expires after about one hour.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. A user can change only their own preferences.

Send only the toggles that changed, inside their group. Toggles left out keep their current value.

Liveness probe used as the hosting platform health check.

Public — no bearer token is needed, and it is exempt from rate limiting.

It reports only that this process is accepting requests. It does not call Supabase or MultiSet, so a 200 says nothing about their health.
